recipes.name: Roasted Tomato Pasta with Feta and Shrimp

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes.

While pasta is cooking, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir in hot oil until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add shrimp; cook, stirring occasionally, until opaque, 3 to 5 minutes. Pour in tomatoes and cook until heated through. Season with basil, salt, and pepper.
Add drained pasta to sauce; toss to coat. Sprinkle with feta to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Tomato Pasta with Feta and Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This roasted tomato pasta recipe is super simple to make with linguine, shrimp, fire-roasted tomatoes, feta, and fresh basil for a beautiful meal for two.

review.reviewBody: I have given 5 star ratings before, but I have to say that this leads them all! Fire roasted tomatoes was pure genious especially when combined with the feta cheese. Because of the salt content in both the tomatoes and the feta cheese, I opted not to add any additional salt. It was not missed, in fact, it was perfect. For a double recipe I used 3 cans of the tomatoes and a pound and a half of the larger (21-25 count) shrimp. Will I make this again? , oh yeah.

This is an excellent, fast and super easy recipe that my family loved. I fire roasted my own tomatoes rather than using canned which was also very easy. The only change I made was to add about a cup of pasta water to the sauce after I'd drained the pasta, but before I added the pasta to the sauce as it seemed a bit dry. Will definitely be adding this to my regular dinner rotation. Thanks for the simple and tasty recipe!

Good but it needs more spice, and it's a bit too salty even without added salt. I might add some vegetables (zucchini, bell pepper, or something) to cut the salt. It definitely makes more than 2 servings as I prepared it. 

When making it, this time, I changed it to up the spices but it still needed more: I partially cooked 1/2 lb shrimp in 2 cloves garlic (for flavor) but added them to the sauce at the end to finish cooking. I did add more spice to the tomatoes -- 1/4 minced onion, 3 cloves garlic, 1/2 large jalapeño, and 1-1/2 tsp dried basil -- and cooked them a bit to meld the flavors. I'm limiting pasta intake, so I served it over brown rice (which was delicious). I'd increase the onions and basil (or add oregano) and use red pepper flakes instead of jalapeño. I might try a bit less feta to cut down on the salt.

I make a very similar recipe. It has been my go to shrimp pasta recipe for years. I saute a small onion in olive oil, then add the garlic cloves for one minute. Then I add the fire roasted tomatoes, 1/2 c. white wine, fresh chopped oregano and some red pepper flakes. I simmer this together for 15 minutes or so. After the pasta is done, I add the shrimp to the sauce and cover the pot. When they have turned pink, I crumble in 4 oz. feta and stir well. Pour it over the pasta, garnish with fresh parsley and serve. Key is not to overcook the shrimp. Cheese does not need to melt, just be distributed well in sauce.

This was very good with some very minor changes. 

1) In the future I will use jumbo shrimp. The recipe calls for medium shrimp. The grocery store only had jumbo shrimp...so the pound was only about 18 shrimp, but by the time they were shelled and cooked they shrunk up. I would prefer the larger shrimp over the small shrimp.

2) My first step after cleaning and shelling was to put the shrimp in a zip-lock bag, pour in a couple of tablespoons of canola oil and mixed in about 6 cloves of fresh garlic and salt. I marinated the shrimp in this for about 2 hours and it made all the difference giving the shrimp an incredible flavor.

3) Recipe calls for 3 cloves garlic. It definitely needs more than that. I minced about 6 or 7 LARGE cloves of garlic.

4) I use fire-roasted diced tomatoes *with garlic* to add more flavor.

5) The editors suggested 3 tbl of fresh basil instead of the one tablespoon in the recipe. I think even more could have been used.

6) For an additional 'kick' I added a few shakes of crushed red pepper and about 1/4 tsp of Ancho chili pepper powder. 

7) I served one portion with feta sprinkled at the end. It was MUCH better mixing it into the pasta before serving to let it melt a bit.

An excellent weeknight meal -- tasty and easy! I like having sauce to dip my bread in so used two cans of fire roasted tomatoes (one regular, one with chilis). I let the tomatoes simmer on low for about 30 minutes. Then I sauted the shrimp in olive oil, 4 cloves minced garlic and heaping 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Once pink, I poured the contents of the shrimp saute into the tomato sauce and stirred in the feta. The suace was thick, creamy and carried a bit of a punch.

This tasted great, and was so quick, hubby couldn't believe it when I told him dinner was ready after just 30 minutes. I used gluten free pasta and I think it sucked up a lot of the sauce, so I add about a 1/2 cup of white wine and it came out perfect.

Not over the top, but good. I had to sauté onion first, just to use them up. Then added more garlic and red pepper flakes, fresh basil and oregano. Added the tomato with a bit of Marsala and let it simmer because I needed a bit more sauce for personal preference. I only had Penne pasta in the pantry so used that. Both the BF and I were happy, especially after a late evening of work. Will do again because we always have most of the ingredients on hand.

This is a good basic recipe, that I took up a notch by adding more spices >>red pepper flakes. more garlic cloves, a little oregano and more basil - also added 1/4 cup white wine, 1/4 cup cream and 2 T cream cheese - it was very good--- I would add more feta next time , but had some in refrigerator already and should of gotten more - I used more shrimp too -I will make again!

Pretty good recipe...I tried it a second time and doubled the recipe. I used one can of regular fire-roasted tomatoes and one can of tex-mex style fire-roasted tomatoes. I also sauteed some onions before adding the shrimp and used garlic powder rather than cloves. Lastly, I added some parmesan cheese to the sauce and pasta.

I made this tonight for the first time. Couldn't have been easier & was delicious. I made a few additions to the recipe just for my own tastes. I sautéed shallot in the olive oil before adding the garlic (love sweetness of shallot & garlic together) and then I did add a few red pepper flakes to kick up the heat a notch. I also used whole wheat linguine. It was so yummy. The feta adds such a nice tang & creaminess to the dish. I can't wait to make this again. Love!!!
I added a can (drained) of artichoke hearts. I didn’t wanna stop eating it. But I only had one portion…
I made this tonight and its was a winner. I used Rotele fire roasted tomatoes with green chilies. And, I doubled the recipe for 3 of us.
This was so easy to make and the fire roasted tomatoes added so much flavor. I was so surprised how good this was. Like a recommendation I did add some Italian seasonings and white wine.
So easy and flavorful. Hubby and I loved the sharp tang of the feta with the shrimp and tomatoes! Will prepare this often!
It was good as is. I also made it again with bullion and whipping cream and mushrooms
This is super easy and tastes great. I added more basil, but cooked everything else with the recipe.
Excellent and easy! I added capers and onions but skipped salt and pepper :)
Very tasty and quick to prepare. I made this with spiralized zucchini and topped with Parmesan cheese. Will definitely make this again.
Delicious and very easy to make! The feta is a really good flavor combination with the fire roasted tomatoes and the shrimp addition isn't too heavy either!
